Individual building square footage and phased MW capacity are not published.

profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Richmond, Virginia mega-campus, spanning Henrico County and Sandston. This is QTS's flagship facility story: in 2010 QTS converted a former semiconductor manufacturing site into what Wikipedia describes as a 1.3 million square foot mega data center.

reading.body:
RIC3 DC2 is one building on QTS's Richmond 3 mega-campus in Sandston, Virginia, a converted semiconductor manufacturing site spanning 221 acres across five planned buildings. The campus is planned for 240 MW total capacity upon completion, but QTS has not published per-building megawatt allocations, so the individual power budget for DC2 is unknown. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, 240 MW across the full campus would support roughly 6,000 racks, though this figure describes the entire campus, not this single building.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 publish power capacity totaling 1,375 MW. The Richmond 3 campus as a whole ranks 24th by published capacity in the state, sitting below the state median of disclosed megawatt figures. QTS publishes the campus total but not individual building capacities, making it impossible to rank RIC2 DC2 independently or to assess what fraction of the 240 MW plan has been deployed versus remains planned.

The building is too new or insufficiently detailed in public sources to carry published certifications for specific workload classes. Its location on a former semiconductor manufacturing site may indicate existing or planned electrical and cooling infrastructure adapted to high-density compute, but no specifics are published. The operator is Blackstone-owned as of August 2021, making the campus part of a hyperscaler-scale capital provider's portfolio, though individual tenant occupancy is not published.
